intro: Venezuela, birthplace of the liberator Simón Bolívar, has the world's largest oil reserves but has suffered a deep crisis in recent years.

chapters.title: Early peoples and conquest
text: Carib, Arawak and other peoples lived here. Spanish explorers, seeing houses on stilts in Lake Maracaibo, named it 'Little Venice'. Spain ruled from the 1500s.

chapters.title: Bolívar and independence
text: Simón Bolívar, born in Caracas in 1783, led wars that freed Venezuela, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru and Bolivia from Spain. Venezuela became fully independent in 1830 when Gran Colombia split.

highlight.title: El Libertador
highlight.text: Bolivia is named after Bolívar, and his name is on Venezuela's currency.

chapters.title: Oil and crisis
text: Oil was found in the 1910s, and by the 1970s Venezuela was one of Latin America's richest countries. Hugo Chávez was elected in 1998 and launched his 'Bolivarian Revolution'. After his death in 2013, Nicolás Maduro took over.

Falling oil output, hyperinflation and repression led nearly eight million people to leave. The 2024 election was widely judged to have been won by the opposition, though Maduro claimed victory. In January 2026 US forces captured Maduro and flew him to New York to face charges.

keyTerms.meaning: The political movement founded by Hugo Chávez.
